```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

niceSMD builds a "Table 1" of descriptive statistics for two or more groups,
with **one absolute standardized mean difference (SMD) per variable**, and
shows it as a formatted table in the console, in Quarto and R Markdown
documents, and in editable Word files.

```{r setup}
library(niceSMD)
d <- example_table1_data()
head(d, 3)
```

## A first table

Name the grouping column and the covariates to summarize. When more than two
groups are present, `group_for_SMD` names the pair the SMD compares; all
groups are still displayed.

```{r first-table}
tab <- nice_SMD_table1(
  d, group = "group",
  covar_names = c("age", "bmi", "sex", "smoking", "stage_code"),
  print_covariate_names = c("Age (years)", "BMI", "Sex", "Smoking", "Stage"),
  categorical_vars = "stage_code",           # numeric codes -> categories
  group_for_SMD = c("Control", "Treatment"),
  show_missing = "if_any",                   # Missing rows only where needed
  notes = "short"                            # compact footnote
)
tab
```

Ending a chunk with the object (as above) prints the formatted table in HTML,
Word, and PDF output. Variable names are bold, categories are indented, and
the footnotes appear below the table.

## What you get back

`tab` is a list. The pieces you will use most:

```{r components}
tab$smd[, c("label", "smd", "status")]   # numeric, unrounded SMDs
tab$groups                               # group sizes
```

## The options you will use most

| Goal | Argument |
|---|---|
| Show a Missing row only for variables that have missing values | `show_missing = "if_any"` |
| Hide or always show all Missing rows | `show_missing = FALSE` / `TRUE` |
| Short, manuscript-style footnote | `notes = "short"` (or `"none"`) |
| Analysis weights | `weights = "analysis_weight"` |
| Complex survey design | `design = survey::svydesign(...)` |
| Fewer or more decimals | `contDigits`, `catDigits`, `smdDigits` |
| Order of group columns | `group_order = c(...)` |

See `?nice_SMD_table1` for every argument with examples.

## Export to Word

```{r word, eval = FALSE}
save_table1_docx(tab, "Table1.docx", landscape = FALSE, font_size = 10)
```

Or pass `docx_path = "Table1.docx"` to `nice_SMD_table1()`. Use
`table1_flextable()` to get an editable `flextable` for further styling.

## Several trials?

For pooled individual participant data from multiple trials, see
`nice_trial_table1()` and the article *Tables by trial and treatment arm*.
